page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.16 is a cloud compute instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads and multi-threaded processing. The virtual machine runs on the x86_64 architecture, powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8167M processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It provides 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs through hyperthreading, coupled with 240.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU, offering high memory density for large in-memory data processing.

The instance operates without local NVMe or SSD storage and lacks integrated GPU acceleration. Storage must be provisioned via remote block volumes or network-attached file storage over the infrastructure network. A complimentary public IPv4 address is included with each deployment. The absence of local disk drives requires reliance on attached network storage for persistent or scratch space, which shifts I/O performance dependencies onto the storage network tier.

From a resource allocation perspective, the high RAM-to-CPU ratio makes this server type cost-efficient for workloads where memory capacity is the primary scaling bottleneck rather than clock frequency. Because the base clock speed is set at 2.0 GHz, the instance prioritizes parallel throughput and memory capacity over extreme single-threaded execution speed. VM.Standard2.16 fits applications including relational databases, in-memory caching systems, enterprise resource planning suites, and batch ETL data pipelines requiring significant working memory.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.16 is an x86_64 virtual server built for memory-heavy and multi-threaded enterprise computing. The instance is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8167M processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, delivering 16 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with two threads per core. System memory totals 240.0 GB, providing an allocation of 7.5 GB per vCPU. The server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address and features no attached local storage or GPU hardware accelerators, necessitating external network-attached block volumes for data persistence. With its elevated memory-to-core ratio and dedicated CPU capacity, the VM.Standard2.16 provides balanced efficiency for memory-constrained deployments where high concurrency and large memory footprints take precedence over peak single-core clock frequencies. Typical workloads appropriate for this configuration include in-memory databases, memory-intensive analytical processing, enterprise software suites, and large-scale ETL data transformation tasks.
